configuration: Template 0.14.0: release coordinates only. Managed files now name Lace 0.1.0-alpha.2: the root package.json Lace dependencies, the LACE_API_IMAGE and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE defaults in .env.example (ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-alpha.2 and ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-alpha.2) and the versioned commands in docs/lace-operations.md and docs/lace-astro-site.md. Generate the target template with your project's site mode and with --cloudflare exactly when your project has Cloudflare files.

Upgrade never edits your .env, README, lace.config.ts, worker/wrangler.jsonc or any file under site/. After applying, set LACE_API_IMAGE and LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE in .env to the 0.1.0-alpha.2 images (or your own compatible overrides); in starter projects run pnpm --dir site add @lacecms/astro@0.1.0-alpha.2 @lacecms/render@0.1.0-alpha.2 @lacecms/sdk@0.1.0-alpha.2 @lacecms/content@0.1.0-alpha.2, and in existing-site mode update the same packages in your own site; then run pnpm install. These coordinates are downloadable only after owner publication.
Template 0.13.0 (included when upgrading from 0.12.0 or earlier):

Template 0.13.0: guidance only. For --cloudflare projects the managed docs/lace-operations.md documents the complete local Worker journey (pointing .env at the local Worker, browser setup, build token and site build), lace doctor --target cloudflare-local and cloudflare-remote, recovery for an expired setup token, an unavailable or rejected deploy hook and restarts, and that deploy hooks require a Git-connected Pages project (or another provider's bodiless build hook); a hook accepted by the provider is recorded as running and is not proof of a successful deploy. The managed Pages workflow gains a comment; projects without Cloudflare receive only the operations-guide version note.

Generate the target template with the same site mode as your project and with --cloudflare exactly when your project has Cloudflare files. Upgrade creates or changes no Worker configuration (worker/wrangler.jsonc stays yours), Cloudflare resource, secret or deployment, and never changes, adds or deletes files under site/. Your README is user-owned; incorporate the new Cloudflare guidance there manually if desired.
Template 0.12.0 (included when upgrading from 0.11.0 or earlier):

Template 0.12.0: --cloudflare now generates a separate CMS Worker in worker/: the managed entry worker/index.ts (it imports lace.config.ts at bundle time), the managed worker/.dev.vars.example and the user-owned worker/wrangler.jsonc. Update @lacecms/cli and install @lacecms/platform-cloudflare and @lacecms/db packages built from Step 31A or later; the packaged admin is not in published 0.1.0-alpha.1 artifacts.

Generate the target template with your site mode and with --cloudflare exactly when your project has Cloudflare files (create-lace <dir> --cloudflare plus --starter, --existing-site <path> or --no-site). For Cloudflare projects the upgrade removes the former Pages-only root wrangler.jsonc when unmodified (an edited copy is a removal conflict; move your edits to worker/wrangler.jsonc or the Pages workflow and restore the file before rerunning), adds worker/index.ts and worker/.dev.vars.example, and replaces the root package.json (Worker dependencies and local cf:* scripts), .env.example, .gitignore, the Pages workflow and the operations guide.

Upgrade never creates or changes the user-owned worker/wrangler.jsonc. Copy it from a freshly generated project of the same release and mode, set your D1 database ID (also in LACE_D1_DATABASE_ID in .env), R2 bucket, optional KV namespace and LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, then run pnpm install and pnpm cf:env:prepare. Add the new Cloudflare settings from .env.example (LACE_WRANGLER_CONFIG=worker/wrangler.jsonc, LACE_CLOUDFLARE_PERSIST_TO=./.lace/data/cloudflare and the D1 ID) to your existing .env manually; preparation never replaces .env.

No Cloudflare resource, secret, migration or deployment is created or changed by upgrade; the Pages workflow keeps deploying only the static site. Projects without Cloudflare files receive only managed guidance and .gitignore changes. Your README is user-owned; incorporate the new Cloudflare Worker guidance there manually if desired.
Template 0.11.0 (included when upgrading from 0.10.0 or earlier):

Template 0.11.0: projects record their site mode in .lace/manifest.json as site: { mode, path } (starter with site, existing with the relative site path, or none). Update @lacecms/cli before upgrading; older CLIs reject the new manifest field. A project without a recorded mode is treated as starter mode with path site and gains the record when the upgrade is applied.

Generate the target template with the same site mode as your project (create-lace <dir> --starter, --existing-site <path> or --no-site); lace upgrade refuses a template generated for another mode or path and names the matching flags. Upgrade keeps the recorded mode and never creates, changes or deletes files under site/ or in an existing site. Changing modes requires generating a fresh project in the new mode and moving configuration manually.

Starter projects receive README/operations guide wording that names the site mode; managed infrastructure is otherwise unchanged. Your README is user-owned; incorporate the new guidance there manually if desired.
Template 0.10.0 (included when upgrading from 0.9.0 or earlier):

Template 0.10.0: the managed docs/lace-astro-site.md and docs/lace-operations.md now use the lace add block command from @lacecms/cli to install, update and scaffold block components. Upgrade updates only those managed guides; it never changes, adds or deletes files under site/.

Optional: after updating @lacecms/cli, run pnpm exec lace add block --all (add --site <path> for a site outside site/) to check your block components against the bundled registry; unchanged files are reported current or updated, and edited components or an edited block map are reported as conflicts and never overwritten. Your README is user-owned; incorporate the new block guidance there manually if desired.
Template 0.9.0 (included when upgrading from 0.8.0 or earlier):

Template 0.9.0: new projects load and render published content through the @lacecms/sdk, @lacecms/render and @lacecms/astro packages with user-owned block components. Upgrade updates only managed files (the operations guide and the new docs/lace-astro-site.md); it never changes, adds or deletes files under site/.
Your site keeps building with its current files. To migrate it manually: generate a fresh 0.9.0 project in a temporary directory with the same create-lace version and compare its site/ with yours.
1. Add @lacecms/astro, @lacecms/render and @lacecms/content next to @lacecms/sdk in site/package.json at the release version, then run pnpm install.
2. Copy site/src/lib/lace.ts, site/src/env.d.ts, site/src/lace/blocks.ts, site/lace.site.json and site/src/components/lace/ from the fresh project.

3. Re-apply your own markup changes from site/src/components/*Block.astro to the matching files in site/src/components/lace/; the new components receive validated data instead of reading block fields themselves. Keep the data-lace-* hooks your styles use.

4. Change each page to call getSite() from src/lib/lace.ts, read entries with byPath('/'), entries('posts') and bySlug('posts', slug), render them with LaceBlocks from @lacecms/astro/LaceBlocks.astro and the blocks map, and type layouts with PublishedEntry from @lacecms/sdk.

5. Delete site/src/lib/site-data.ts, site/src/lib/rendering.ts, site/src/lib/rich-text.ts, site/src/components/BlockRenderer.astro, the RichText*.astro components and the old block components, then run pnpm typecheck and pnpm build.

Rich text and URLs are now validated with the CMS rules: content the old site copy accepted but the CMS rejects (such as https:example.com or a paragraph inside a paragraph) fails the build with its model, entry, block and field. To connect an existing Astro site instead of the starter, follow docs/lace-astro-site.md.
Template 0.8.0 (included when upgrading from 0.7.0 or earlier):

Template 0.8.0: review the managed deploy/nginx.conf change, which sends Cache-Control: no-cache for served site responses so browsers revalidate after a release switch, then recreate the web service. The proxy and operations-guide changes need no new API, admin, CLI or builder artifacts; Admin publication-visibility guidance appears with compatible freshly built Step 29B or later admin artifacts.

Site source stays user-owned and is not changed by upgrade. To see publications on reload in Astro dev, optionally adopt the generated pattern: revalidate the build export with its ETag in development while keeping one memoized export per static build, and read the current post by slug instead of getStaticPaths props. New or renamed slugs still need an Astro dev restart. See docs/lace-operations.md for each publication visibility mode.
Template 0.7.0 (included when upgrading from 0.6.0 or earlier):

Use compatible freshly built Step 29A or later API, admin, CLI and builder artifacts; previously published alpha artifacts do not acquire this behavior. No package or image is published by this upgrade.

Review managed Compose and environment changes. Set LACE_BUILD_SOURCE_ROOT to the host installation root containing pnpm-lock.yaml, LACE_BUILD_SITE_DIR to the relative Astro directory and LACE_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR to its relative static output. Generated defaults are ., site and dist. For an existing standalone Astro root above cms/, use .., . and dist.

Set LACE_BUILD_SITE_ID and LACE_BUILD_SITE_LABEL to safe operator-authored names shared by API and builder, then recreate the affected services. Current identity is configuration, not verification of a successful deployment.

Preserve user-owned README, lace.config.ts and site source. Retain existing managed-file conflict review; incorporate applicable instructions in an existing README manually. The last static release remains served until a selected-source build succeeds. See docs/lace-operations.md for external workspace and SDK integration prerequisites.
